fact: 1921年3月8日至16日，俄共（布）第十次代表大会在莫斯科召开，列宁作关于以实物税代替余粮收集制的报告，大会通过决议正式决定从战时共产主义过渡到新经济政策（NEP）。列宁称1921年春天的危机是「我们计划……用无产阶级国家直接下命令的办法，在一个小农国家里按共产主义原则来调整国家的产品生产和分配。现实生活说明我们错了」。

sources.title: 中国社会科学院俄罗斯东欧中亚研究所，新经济政策
sources.quote: 1921年3月,俄共(布)'十大'召开,列宁在会上作了关于以实物税代替余粮收集制的报告。根据列宁的报告大会通过决议,决定废止余粮收集制实行粮食税。从此,开始了从战时共产主义政策向新经济政策的过渡。

sources.title: 百度百科，新经济政策
sources.quote: 1921年3月,布尔什维克党的第十次代表大会通过了由战时共产主义过渡到新经济政策的决议。新经济政策以粮食税代替征收,允许农民自由出卖余粮,允许私商自由贸易、并且将一部分小工厂还给私人,还准备把一些企业租给外国资本家。

fact: 1921年3月21日，全俄中央执行委员会颁布《关于以实物税代替余粮收集制》法令，废除强制性余粮收集制（prodrazvyorstka），代之以固定的粮食税（prodnalog）。税额远低于余粮收集制：1920—1921年度通过余粮收集制征收谷物3.67亿普特，而1921—1922年度通过粮食税仅征2.40亿普特。农民交税后可自由出售剩余农产品。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Prodnalog
sources.quote: Prodnalog replaced prodrazvyorstka (introduced in 1919) and was introduced by a Decree of the All-Russian Central Executive Committee on March 21, 1921. ... in 1920-1921 the peasants surrendered to the state 367 million poods (6,010,000 metric tons) of cereals through prodrazvyorstka, as opposed to 240 million poods (3,930,000 metric tons) in 1921-1922 through prodnalog. After paying the tax, the peasants were allowed to trade the surplus.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院俄罗斯东欧中亚研究所，新经济政策
sources.quote: 1921年3月21日颁布《关于以实物税代替余粮收集制》法令,规定农民交纳粮食税后,剩余的粮食等农产品可以到市场交换物品。粮食税的税额比余粮收集制大为减少,1921—1922年度全国税额比上年度减少43.3%。

fact: 1921年3月1日至18日，波罗的海舰队基地喀琅施塔得的水兵与平民发动反布尔什维克起义（喀琅施塔得叛乱），由斯捷潘·彼得里琴科领导。叛乱者要求重新自由选举苏维埃、经济自由、取消贸易限制、释放政治犯等。3月5日布尔什维克发出最后通牒，3月18日红军经冰面攻占要塞，数千叛乱者被枪决或监禁。列宁称此危机「无疑比邓尼金、尤登尼奇和高尔察克加起来还危险」。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Kronstadt rebellion
sources.quote: For sixteen days in March 1921, rebels in Kronstadt's naval fortress rose in opposition to the Soviet government which they had helped to consolidate. Led by Stepan Petrichenko... the authorities took an uncompromising stance, presenting an ultimatum demanding unconditional surrender on March 5... suppressed the revolt on March 18 after shooting and imprisoning several thousand rebels. According to Lenin, the crisis was the most critical the Bolsheviks had yet faced, 'undoubtedly more dangerous than Denikin, Yudenich, and Kolchak combined'.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院俄罗斯东欧中亚研究所，喀琅施塔得叛乱
sources.quote: 于1921年2月28日发动'叛乱'。他们在3月2日的集会上谴责共产党血腥毁灭的三年。要求举行新的完全自由的秘密选举,要求言论自由,出版和集会自由,'没有布尔什维克的苏维埃',平等分配食物,取消贸易限制……

fact: 1921年夏，严重干旱席卷伏尔加河流域，引发1921—1922年大饥荒。官方统计约3600万农民受灾，死亡人数估计在200万至500万之间（一说高达1000万）。1921年7月，高尔基向国际红十字会主席南森发出求援电报；国联拒绝援助共产主义政权，南森转向美国胡佛领导的美国救济总署（ARA）。

sources.title: EBSCO Research Starters, Famine in Russia Claims Millions of Lives
sources.quote: In July of 1921, the noted Soviet revolutionary writer Maxim Gorky sent an appeal to Fridtjof Nansen, director of the International Red Cross, detailing the desperate situation in the Volga provinces and asking for international aid. Nansen appealed to the League of Nations, which refused to supply aid to Russia as long as the Communist regime held power. He then informed Gorky that the only other possible source of aid on the scale required was the United States and directed the appeal to Herbert Hoover.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Russian famine of 1921–1922
sources.quote: An official Soviet publication of the early 1920s concluded that about five million deaths occurred in 1921 from famine and related disease... some sources spoke of ten million dead.

fact: 1921年8月，美国救济总署（ARA）与苏俄政府在里加达成救济协议：美方提供谷物与督导人员，苏俄承担大部分分配费用，美方承诺不干涉苏俄政治。12月22日美国国会通过法案拨款2000万美元购买玉米和种子粮。12月30日ARA与苏俄政府在伦敦签订购粮合同，苏联动用黄金储备（约1200万美元）购买粮食。到1922年8月，ARA每天为约1050万苏俄公民提供食物。

sources.title: Wilson Center, Herbert Hoover's Brush with Bolshevism
sources.quote: This came about on December 22, 1921, when the U.S. Congress passed a bill authorizing an appropriation of $20 million for the purchase of corn and seed grain from American farmers for Russian relief. To this total was added other government money and private donations (as well as the expenditure of about $12 million from the Soviet government's gold reserve), and in the end the two-year ARA mission was backed by over $60 million... The height of ARA activity was reached in August 1922, when American kitchens were feeding white bread, beans, corn grits, and cocoa to about 10 1/2 million Soviet citizens a day.

sources.title: 中国社会科学院俄罗斯东欧中亚研究所，美国对苏维埃俄国的饥荒援助
sources.quote: 1921年12月30日,布罗温和克拉辛在伦敦签订了美国救济总署与苏维埃政府之间关于在美国购买谷物的合同。在这份合同中苏维埃政府承诺,购买的粮食将只用于救济伏尔加流域的饥民。

fact: 1921年6月，23岁的美国企业家阿曼德·哈默抵达苏俄，原计划提供医疗援助，但发现饥荒更为紧迫，遂以100万美元在美国购买小麦运往苏俄。列宁在克里姆林宫接见哈默，说服他放弃从医、接管西伯利亚一座石棉矿——这是苏俄授予的第一个外国租让企业。哈默后来还说服亨利·福特等美国资本家进入苏俄市场。

sources.title: 中国社会科学院俄罗斯东欧中亚研究所，苏联新经济政策-历史发展
sources.quote: 1921年,阿曼德·哈默才23岁……这年6月,他克服种种困难,来到了苏俄。……不久,哈默就成了第一个在苏俄经营租让企业的美国人。

sources.title: The New York Times, Hammer's Kremlin Connection（1973-05-20）
sources.quote: Lenin was delighted with the ingenuity of the young American and in October, 1921, persuaded him to forget doctoring and take over a ramshackle asbestos mine in the mountains of western Siberia, the first foreign concession to be granted by the Soviets. Dr. Hammer and his brothers... finally were reaping a profit of several hundred thousand dollars a year before they sold the mine back to the Russians in 1926.

fact: 1921年5月，莫斯科一磅面包售价约3000卢布（两周前为1800卢布），一磅糖售价18000卢布。据《观察家报》引述《泰晤士报》记者，莫斯科一条两磅面包2000卢布、一磅黄油18000卢布、一码布100000卢布。克里姆林宫是「全俄唯一感受不到饥饿的地方」，高官通过「外交行李」从拉脱维亚和爱沙尼亚每周两次进口食品。

sources.title: The New York Times, Moscow Near Famine, Plague in Provinces（1921-05-26）
sources.quote: A pound of bread sold for 1,800 rubles two weeks ago, and it is declared that the price today is 3,000 rubles. Sugar is selling at 18,000 rubles per pound. The Kremlin... is said to be the only place in Russia where hunger is not felt.

sources.title: The Spectator, The Russian Tragedy（1921-04-16）
sources.quote: The prices charged—2,000 roubles for a pound loaf, 18,000 roubles for a pound of butter, 100,000 roubles for a yard of cloth—show that the currency is debased beyond repair, and that the normal trading system has broken down.

fact: 1921年初彼得格勒配给标准：冶金车间工人每日800克黑面包、突击工人600克、持A.V.卡工人400克、其他工人200克；但实际发放经常不足额且不规律。运输工人日均摄入仅700—1000卡路里。1920年彼得格勒工人工资仅为1913年的8.6%—9%。取暖靠拆烧门窗地板，上下水管道爆裂。

sources.title: Paul Avrich, Kronstadt 1921（PDF）
sources.quote: at the beginning of 1921, the workers of Petrograd's metal-smelting shops and blast furnaces received a daily ration of 800 grams of black bread, while shock workers received 600 grams, and lesser categories only 400 or even 200 grams. But even this meager allotment was doled out on an irregular basis. The diet of transport workers was said to average between 700 and 1,000 calories a day... By the end of 1920 the real wages of factory workers in Petrograd had, according to official estimates, fallen to 8.6 percent of their pre-war levels.

sources.title: The Spectator, The Russian Tragedy（1921-04-16）
sources.quote: Doors, door-posts, window-sashes, flooring—all have been torn up for fuel; the water and sewage pipes have all burst... The inhabitants spend much of their time in trying to supplement these miserable rations by bartering clothes or boots for milk or flour.

fact: 1917年至1921年间，彼得格勒人口从244万降至约70万（减少约三分之二），莫斯科人口减少约44.5%—50%。工人从1919年的300万降至1921年的约112.5万。城市居民用衣物靴子换食品，「口袋人」（meshochnik）往返城乡之间贩运粮食。工厂缺勤率约50%。

sources.title: The Spectator, The Russian Tragedy（1921-04-16）
sources.quote: the population, according to a Bolshevik census, has declined from 2,440,000 in 1917 to 705,000. Two-thirds of the inhabitants have fled to the villages or have died of hunger and disease.

sources.title: Pierre Broué, The History of the Bolshevik Party, Chapter VII
sources.quote: In autumn 1920 the population of forty provincial capitals had fallen by 33% from the 1917 level... In three years Petrograd lost 57.5% and Moscow lost 44.5% of their population... In 1919 there had been three million workers in industry; in 1920 there were only 1,500,000 and in 1921 1,125,000. 'Normal' absenteeism in the factories was 50%.

fact: 1921年NEP法令确立的法律框架：粮食税代替余粮收集制，农民纳税后余粮可自由交易；废除国家配给制和国家贸易垄断制，实行自由贸易；1921年5月将部分小企业发还原主，7月决定把一批中小工厂和商店租借给本国合作社或个人。租让制企业由私人经营、所有权归国家，承租者须接受国家监督、按期交纳租金和利润分成。

sources.title: 中国社会科学院俄罗斯东欧中亚研究所，新经济政策
sources.quote: 第一,农业方面:1921年3月21日颁布《关于以实物税代替余粮收集制》法令……第二,工业方面:……1921年5月,国家把一部分小企业发还原主经营。7月又决定把一批中小工厂和商店租借给本国的合作社或个人。这些租让和租借企业由私人经营,所有权属于国家。承租者必须接受国家监督指导,遵守苏维埃法令,按期交纳租金和一定比例的利润。第三,流通方面:废除国家配给制和国家贸易垄断制……实行自由贸易制。

sources.title: Wikipedia, New Economic Policy
sources.quote: The Soviet authorities partially revoked the complete nationalization of industry and introduced a mixed economy which allowed private individuals to own small and medium-sized enterprises, while the state continued to control large industries, banks and foreign trade.

fact: NEP并未放松政治管控。契卡（Cheka）在1921年继续大规模镇压反革命与「投机倒把」：捷尔任斯基不仅负责枪决还负责运输，NEP后新增任务是打击「耐普曼」资本家。1921年2月契卡报告全国155起农民起义。外国人在苏俄经营须通过租让合同获得许可，承租者须接受国家监督，合同到期须完好交还企业。政治身份（党员、工人、农民）直接决定配给等级与法律待遇。

sources.title: Pierre Broué, The History of the Bolshevik Party, Chapter VII
sources.quote: The Cheka, the state Communist Party secret police, reported 118 peasant uprisings in February 1921.

sources.title: 中文马克思主义文库，列宁传·国务活动中的盐
sources.quote: 耐普不仅没有限制他的活动,反而对他的活动又提出了新的要求,这就是要同那些刚一去掉了压在头上的战时共产主义的压迫就冒出来的资本家耐普曼作斗争。……1921年8月,苏维埃政府同意把顿巴斯的中小矿场租给私人企业家。

fact: 苏俄纸卢布急剧贬值：1917年1金卢布合7.85纸卢布，到1920年至少合10000纸卢布。1920年一年内面包价格上涨超过10倍。黑市价格是法定价格的40—50倍。物物交换（barter）广泛取代货币成为交换媒介，约90%的工资以实物而非货币支付。重工业产值仅为1913年的20%。

sources.title: Paul Avrich, Kronstadt 1921（PDF）
sources.quote: During 1920 alone the price of bread increased more than tenfold. ... a gold ruble worth 7 paper rubles and 85 kopecks in 1917 brought at least 10,000 paper rubles three years later. ... As the value of money drained away, an increasing proportion of wages was paid to the workers in kind.

sources.title: Wikipedia, War communism
sources.quote: The ruble collapsed, with barter increasingly replacing money as a medium of exchange and, by 1921, heavy industry output had fallen to 20% of 1913 levels. ... 90% of wages were paid with goods rather than money.

fact: 1921年苏俄工业崩溃程度：重工业产量仅为1913年的20%，生铁产量为1913年的1.6%、钢为2.4%；煤产量从1913年的2750万吨降至1920年的700万吨；60%的机车停运，63%的铁路无法使用。1921年工业工人从1919年的300万降至112.5万。工厂普遍缺乏原料与燃料，靠烧木材运行火车。

sources.title: Pierre Broué, The History of the Bolshevik Party, Chapter VII
sources.quote: Industry produced 20% in quantity of its prewar production, and 13% in value. The output of iron represented 1.6% and that of steel 2.4%. ... 60% of locomotives were out of action and 63% of the railway tracks could not be used.

sources.title: Wikipedia, War communism
sources.quote: Coal production decreased from 27.5 million tons (1913) to 7 million tons (1920), while overall factory production also declined from 10,000 million roubles to 1,000 million roubles. ... 70% of locomotives were in need of repair.

fact: NEP实施后私人贸易迅速复兴。耐普曼（NEPman）商人阶层崛起，从事消费品批发与零售。「口袋人」（meshochnik）从农村收购粮食到城市贩卖；到1920年底非法贸易已基本取代官方分配渠道。黑市价格是法定价格的40—50倍。1921年8月苏维埃政府同意把顿巴斯中小矿场租给私人企业家以提高煤产量。

sources.title: Paul Avrich, Kronstadt 1921（PDF）
sources.quote: A black market quickly sprang into being. Swarms of 'bagmen' tramped from village to village, buying bread and vegetables which they would sell or barter to the famished inhabitants of the cities. By the end of 1920 illicit trade had grown to such proportions that it largely supplanted the official channels of distribution.

sources.title: Pierre Broué, The History of the Bolshevik Party, Chapter VII
sources.quote: there was a black market, in which the prices were forty to fifty times higher than the legal prices.

fact: 1921—1922年饥荒期间，伏尔加地区出现大规模营养不良、霍乱和斑疹伤寒流行。ARA医疗部门分发了超过12.5万件医疗包裹、1500万磅医疗物资，为640万人接种疫苗、130万人种痘。手术在无暖气手术室无麻醉条件下进行，伤口用报纸或破布包扎。难民中大量孤儿被集中到无供暖仓库。

sources.title: Wikipedia, Russian famine of 1921–1922
sources.quote: There were 125,000 medical packages, weighing 15 million pounds, sent on 69 ships. ... Operations were performed in unheated operating rooms without anesthetics and often with bare hands. Wounds were dressed with newspapers or rags. ... Number of inoculations given 6,396,598. Number of vaccinations given 1,304,401.

sources.title: Wilson Center, Herbert Hoover's Brush with Bolshevism
sources.quote: Thousands of refugees dying of starvation huddled on the outskirts of every major town, and piles of emaciated corpses lay unburied in cemeteries. Authorities gathered abandoned and orphaned children into unheated warehouses, where they lay in rags on bare boards; for many, food meant bread made from straw and acorns.
